Laging handa ang Quezon City sa anumang sakuna. 🌧

Bilang paghahanda sa posibleng epekto ng Bagyong #UwanPH, naglatag ang Quezon City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (QCDRRMO) ng mga strategic staging areas sa bawat distrito.

Naka-preposition sa mga ito ang mga kagamitan at tauhan mula sa QCDRRMO, Traffic and Transport Management Department, Task Force Disiplina, QC Police District, at Department of Public Order and Safety.

Kaagapay rin ng QC ang ilang tauhan ng Armed Forces of the Philippines at Philippine Coast Guard.

Handang mag-deploy ng karagdagang personnel ang QC para agad na tugunan ang pangangailangan ng mga mamamayan at matiyak ang kaligtasan ng QCitizens.

🚨🇵🇭 A MILLION EVACUATE AS SUPER TYPHOON APPROACHES THE PHILIPPINE CAPITAL

Nearly one million people are being evacuated as Super Typhoon Fung-wong barrels toward Luzon, the island where Manila sits, with winds strong enough to turn trees into projectiles and shred buildings.

Just days ago, Typhoon Tino slammed into Cebu, killing hundreds and knocking out power across the central Philippines. 

Much of the country's still in the dark, and now they’re watching another monster storm approach from the east.

Typhoon Fung-wong is expected to tear through the capital within hours, with up to 3 meters of flooding forecast near the island’s coast.

Source: TRT World

🇵🇭 PHILIPPINES BRACES FOR ANOTHER SUPER TYPHOON

Just days after Typhoon Tino wrecked Cebu and killed over 200 people, another monster is on the way to the Philippines, and this one’s aiming for the island that holds Manila.

Typhoon Fung-wong, locally named Uwan, is spinning with winds up to 185 kph and could slam into Luzon on Sunday night.

The last storm left half a million people in the dark, with power outages across central islands that could take weeks to fix.

A storm of that magnitude will likely tear through the nation's capital, where millions of people are barely coming to terms with the last typhoon.

data.text:
Hello everyone! With 𝐒𝐮𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐲𝐩𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐧 𝐔𝐰𝐚𝐧 affecting several areas tonight, we want to remind everyone to 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐲 𝐬𝐚𝐟𝐞, 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐲 𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐲 𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐫𝐭. Please take a moment to read and check your area’s status.

AREAS TO TAKE NOTE OF:
🔴 RED Warning – Take Action Now
Metro Manila, Rizal, Quezon, and Laguna
• Serious and life-threatening flooding is expected
• If your area is flood-prone, prepare to evacuate early
• Move to higher ground and secure important items

🟠 ORANGE Warning – Be Prepared
Batangas, Cavite, Bulacan, parts of Laguna, Nueva Ecija, and Quezon
• Flooding is likely and may worsen
• Keep your go-bag ready and monitor announcements
• Charge devices and secure your home

🟡 YELLOW Warning – Stay Alert
Pampanga, Tarlac, Zambales, Bataan, parts of Nueva Ecija
• Possible flooding in low-lying areas
• Stay informed and avoid unnecessary travel

𝐀 𝐅𝐞𝐰 𝐒𝐚𝐟𝐞𝐭𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐓𝐨𝐧𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭
• Charge phones, powerbanks, and emergency lights
• Prepare a small go-bag with essentials (IDs, water, meds, flashlight, cash, food)
• Stay indoors as much as possible

Pinulong ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) at Office of Civil Defense-National Capital Region ang iba’t- ibang ahensiya ng pamahalaan, kabilang ang Metro Manila local government units (LGUs) para tiyakin na handa ang lahat sa posibleng pinsalang dala ng bagyong #UwanPH.

Sa pagpupulong na pinangunahan ni Atty. Crisanto Saruca, Jr. ng MMDA Metropolitan Public Safety Office at OCD-NCR Regional Director George Keyser, iniulat ng bawat ahensiya at LGUs ang kanilang mga preparasyon sa pagtugon sa emergencies ngayong may bagyo.

Sa hanay ng MMDA, naka-preposition na ang Search and Rescue (SAR) teams sa iba't ibang quadrants ng Metro Manila at ang mga kagamitan tulad ng mga rubber boats, mobile pump units, ring bouys, puddles, throw ropes, at iba pa sakaling kailanganin para sa rescue operations.

Handa rin ang Quick Response Team ng Department of Public Works and Highways.

Kasama sa ibang paghahanda ng mga lokal na pamahalaan ng Metro Manila ang pagsasagawa ng Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment, paglilinis ng drainage, pagpuputol ng mga puno at iba pa, upang maiwasan ang pagbabaha at sakuna sa Kamaynilaan.

Tuloy-tuloy naman ang declogging operations ng MMDA upang tanggalin ang mga basura na bumabara sa mga kanal.

Siniguro rin ng MMDA na lahat ng 71 pumping stations ng ahensiya ay fully operational.

24/7 naman nakasubaybay ang MMDA para sa monitoring ng weather updates at lagay ng mga pangunahing kalsada sa Metro Manila.

Kasama sa pagpupulong ang mga kinatawan mula sa National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council, Department of Transportation, Department of the Interior and Local Government, Department of Social Welfare and Development, Bureau of Fire Protection, at Philippine Coast Guard.

3.⁠ Trump floated the idea of 50-year mortgages to make housing affordable for young buyers - a potential game-changer that could slash payments and reshape U.S homeownership like FDR’s 30-year model once did.

4.⁠ Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said he’ll meet Secretary Rubio only if Moscow’s demands are met - a diplomatic maybe wrapped in a power play after Trump-Putin talks collapsed over Ukraine.

5.⁠ Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa arrived in Washington for a historic meeting with Trump - the first Syrian leader ever to set foot in the White House, and a diplomatic shockwave decades in the making.

6.⁠ SpaceX launched 29 more Starlink satellites from Florida, marking a record 28th flight for the Falcon 9 booster as Elon’s internet empire keeps expanding.

7.⁠ A helicopter crash in Dagestan killed five senior engineers from Russia’s Kizlyar Electromechanical Plant - a major defense supplier - dealing a huge blow to Moscow’s war production just as its air campaign intensifies.

8.⁠ Myanmar’s military leveled KK Park - a notorious cyber-slavery hub where trafficked workers ran global romance scams, faced torture, and were trapped in a real-life digital hell.

9.⁠ Joe Rogan called Zohran Mamdani’s victory speech “a lot like communism,” warning that the new NYC mayor’s call for bigger government sounds more like ideology than a plan to help ordinary people.

10.⁠ Nearly one million people are being evacuated as Super Typhoon Fung-wong hurtles toward Luzon - home to the Philippine capital, Manila - with catastrophic winds and up to three meters of coastal flooding expected.
